Rashi on Shabbat 148b:10:1.hebrew: אם לאו אינו משמט - אלמא ניתנה ליתבע. ומשני: מאי אינו משמט? דאי יהיב ליה, שקיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:10:1.english: If not, it does not cancel [the loan] - Evidently, it can be claimed. And [the Gemara] answers: What [is meant by] "it does not cancel"? That if [the borrower] gives [the money] to him, he may take [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:11:1.english: By inference that [in] the first clause, if he gives [it] to him, he may not take [it] - [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:11:2.hebrew: רישא - דהלואת שביעית היא, אי נמי יהיב ליה לוה, צריך למימר ליה מלוה: "משמט אני":
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:11:2.english: The first clause - Since it is a loan of the Sabbatical year, even if the borrower gives [it] to him, the lender must say to him: "I relinquish [the debt]."

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:12:1.hebrew: ואם אמר - לוה "אעפ"כ איני חפץ שישמטו" — יקבל ממנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:12:1.english: And if [he] says - [The] borrower [says to him]: "Nonetheless, I do not want them to remit [it]," he may accept [it] from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:12:2.hebrew: דבר השמטה - אפילו מקבל חובו, יזכיר לו שמיטה בדבורו:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:12:2.english: The word [devar] of the release - Even [when] he accepts [repayment of] his debt, he must mention the release to him verbally.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:13:1.hebrew: שקיל משכונא - בשעת הלואה מהלואת יו"ט:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:13:1.english: [He] would take collateral - At the time of the loan, for a Festival loan.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:13:2.hebrew: מערים איערומי - לאחר י"ט, לוקח ממנו שום חפץ ומעכבו:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:13:2.english: Would circumvent - After the Festival, he takes some object from him and holds onto it.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:14:1.hebrew: פסחו בשבת - אם חל י"ד בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:14:1.english: His Paschal lamb on Shabbat - If the fourteenth [of Nisan] falls on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:14:2.hebrew: וחגיגתו ביו"ט - ביום הקרבתה מותר להקדיש. ואע"ג דתנן: אלו הן משום שבות — אין מקדישין, הני כיון דהקרבתן דוחה, קדושתן דוחה:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:14:2.english: And his Festival peace-offering on the Festival - On the day of its offering it is permitted to consecrate [it]. And even though we learned [in a Mishnah]: "These are [prohibited] on account of shevut — one may not consecrate," [regarding] these [offerings], since their offering overrides [the prohibition], their consecration [also] overrides [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:15:1.english: With [a case where] one registers others with him - As it is written (Exodus 12:4): "According to the number of souls."

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:15:2.english: For his Paschal lamb - For it was already consecrated from yesterday.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:17:1.hebrew: אקדושי - מקדיש ליה רועה מע"ש, שהרי יודע שזה סומך עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:17:1.english: Consecrating [it] - The shepherd consecrates it for him on Shabbat eve, since he knows that this [person] relies upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:17:2.english: Elevation - A mere elevation [in status], that the owners consecrate [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:18:1.hebrew: הא - דקתני אין מקדישין, בחובות שאין קבוע להן זמן קאי, שאין הקרבתן דוחה שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:18:1.english: This [mishna] - which teaches "one may not consecrate," refers to obligations that do not have a set time, for their offering does not override Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:2.hebrew: אבל לא מן הכתב - אם כתב מע"ש: כך וכך אורחים, פלוני ופלוני זמנתי, כדי שלא ישכחם — לא יקרא באותו כתב בשבת. ובגמ' מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:2.english: But not from a written [list] - If he wrote on Shabbat eve, "Such-and-such [a number of] guests, so-and-so and so-and-so I have invited," so that he would not forget them, he may not read from that document on Shabbat. And in the Gemara [it] explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:3.hebrew: מפיס - לשון פייס, מטיל פייס לחלק מי מגיע כל מנה ומנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:3.english: Draws lots [mefis] - An expression of payis [lot]; he casts a lot to divide [and determine] to whom each and every portion goes.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:4.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יתכוין לעשות כו' - שיהו המנות שוות, ולא תהא אחת גדולה ואחת קטנה, לזכות בגדולה הזוכה ע"פ הגורל, והמתחייב ע"פ הגורל לקטנה יטלנה. ובגמ' מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:4.english: As long as he does not intend to make, etc. - [Meaning] that the portions should be equal, and one should not be large and one small, for the one who wins by the lot to acquire the large [portion] and the one assigned the small [portion] by the lot to take it. And in the Gemara, it explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:6.english: For the sanctified [foods] - Among the priests.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:19:7.english: But not for the portions - In the Gemara, [it] explains [this].

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:1:1.hebrew: ואתי לידי סחיטה - ודקאמר במסכת ביצה ניפרוס סודרא עלויה כו', [התם] בדבר יבש קא מיירי:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:1:1.english: And [one] may come to squeezing - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in Tractate Beitzah, "Let us spread a cloth over it, etc.," there it is speaking of a dry substance.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:1:3.hebrew: זימנין דמיפסק כו' - כיון דמצרכת ליה כיסוי, קטר ליה בכד, וזימנין דמיפסק ואתי למקטריה, והיא קשר של קיימא דאסור מדאורייתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:1:3.english: Sometimes it is severed, etc. - Since you require him [to use] a lid, he ties it to the pitcher, and sometimes it is severed and he comes to tie it, which is a permanent knot that is prohibited by Torah law.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:1.english: One may not clap - [Striking] palm against palm because of mourning.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:3.hebrew: מרקדין - לשמחה, וטעמא מפרש במסכת ביצה: שמא יתקן כלי שיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:3.english: Dance - For joy; and the reason is explained in Tractate Beitzah: lest one repair a musical instrument.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:4.hebrew: אפומא דלחייא - לפי שאין ניכר כל כך בין מבוי לרה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:4.english: At the entrance of the sidepost - Because [the boundary] between the alleyway and the public domain is not so recognizable.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:5.hebrew: ואתי לאתויי - חפץ המתגלגל תוך ד' אמות. ומגנדר חצביהן ומייתין ליה, ל"ג:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:2:5.english: And he comes to bring - an object that rolls within four cubits. [The reading] "and their jugs roll and they bring it" — we do not read [this].

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:4:1.english: It is on Shabbat that it is prohibited - to say "lend me," because of writing.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:4:2.hebrew: הא בחול שרי - ולא חיישינן לרבית, ואף על גב דבלשון הלואה קאמר ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:4:2.english: But on a weekday it is permitted - And we are not concerned about interest, even though [one] says it using the language of lending.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:5:1.hebrew: באתרא דקיץ דמייהו - דככרות, לא אתי לידי רבית, שאם יוקירו יתן דמיהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:5:1.english: In a place where their price is set - [That is, the price] of the loaves; it does not lead to interest, for if they become more expensive, he will pay their value.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:6:1.hebrew: לא ניתנה ליתבע - בב"ד, שאין ב"ד נזקקין לה לעולם:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:6:1.english: Cannot be claimed - In court, for the court never attends to it.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:7:1.english: In judgment and [before] a judge - Not to come to judgment, and not to select a judge and trouble himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:8:1.hebrew: השוחט את הפרה וחילקה בראש השנה - של מוצאי שביעית, ללוקחים ובהקפה. וקיי"ל שביעית משמטת בסופה, דכתיב מקץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:8:1.english: One who slaughters a cow and divides it on Rosh HaShana - of [the year] following the Sabbatical year, to purchasers and on credit. And it is established for us [that] the Sabbatical year cancels [debts] at its end, as it is written, "At the end [of seven years]."

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:8:2.hebrew: אם היה חדש - אלול מעובר ועשו ראש השנה שני ימים, משמט, דיום טוב ראשון של סוף שביעית היה, ונמצאת זו הלואת שביעית. ואם לאו, הויא לה הלואת מוצאי שביעית, ואינו משמט:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:8:2.english: If the month was - [if] Elul was full and they observed Rosh Hashanah [for] two days, it cancels [the debt], for the first day of the festival was at the end of the Sabbatical year, and thus this is found to be a loan of the Sabbatical year. And if not, it is a loan of the post-Sabbatical year, and it does not cancel [the debt].

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:9:1.hebrew: <abbr title="לא גרסינן">ל"ג</abbr> אי אמרת בשלמא כו', <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: ואם לא ניתנה ליתבע, מאי משמט? הואיל ואין <abbr title="בית דין">ב"ד</abbr> נזקקין לכופו, שמוטה היא ועומדת:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:9:1.english: We do not read "Granted, if you say, etc."; rather, this is the text: "And if it cannot be claimed, what is [the meaning of] 'cancels'?" — since the court does not attend to compel him [to pay], it is already canceled.

Rashi on Shabbat 148b:9:2.hebrew: דחול הוא - שהרי חדש מעובר, ולא הוי יו"ט עד למחר. הלכך, אי לאו דשביעית הוא, הוה גבי:
Rashi on Shabbat 148b:9:2.english: That it is a weekday - For the month [of Elul] was intercalated, and the Festival was not until the next day. Therefore, were it not for the Sabbatical [year], he would have collected [it].

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:16:1.hebrew: והא אנן תנן אין נימנין כו' - פירש ה"ר פורת בשם רבינו שמואל דל"ג ליה: חדא, דמה שייך להקשות מנמנין של רשות לנמנין של מצוה? ועוד, דמפרש התם בביצה פרק אין צדין (ביצה דף כז:): מאי "אין נמנין"? אין פוסקין דמים בתחילה לבהמה ביו"ט — "הרי אני עמך בסלע", "הריני עמך בשתים"; אבל אומר לו: "הריני עמך לשליש ולרביע":
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:16:1.english: "But we learned [in a Mishnah]: One may not register, etc." - Rabbi Porat explained in the name of Rabbeinu Shmuel that we do not have this reading: First, what relevance is there to raise an objection from registering [for a meal] of a discretionary nature to registering [for a meal] of a mitzvah? Furthermore, it explains there in Beitzah, in the chapter [entitled] Ein Tzadin (Beitzah 27b): What is [the meaning of] "one may not register"? One may not fix a monetary price initially for an animal on a Festival [by saying], "I am with you for a sela," [or] "I am with you for two [selaim]"; rather, he says to him, "I am with you for a third or for a fourth".

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:19:1.hebrew: מטילין חלשים על הקדשים ביו"ט - תימה, דאמר בפרק ב' דקדושין (דף נג. ושם) דאין חולקין זבחים כנגד זבחים ומנחה כנגד מנחה, ומפיק לה מ"לכל בני אהרן תהיה איש כאחיו". ועוד, דפריך התם מ"והצנועים מושכין ידיהם והגרגרנים חולקין" — מאי "חולקין"? חוטפין, כו'. ואומר רבי, דאין מועלת בהם חלוקה וגורל שיהא ממונו לקדש בו את האשה ולהוציאו בדיינים; אבל מ"מ מטילין היו חלשין לתת לכל א' חלקו, פן יריבו ביחד, כדכתיב (הושע ד): "ועמך כמריבי כהן". והא דמשני התם "חולקין" — לאו דוקא, אלא חוטפין; ולא משני הכי משו' ד"חולקין" משמע כופין לחלוק, ע"כ מחמת שחוטפין אותן שאינן שלהם. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:19:1.english: They cast lots for sanctified foods on a Festival - This is astonishing, for [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Kiddushin (53a, and [elsewhere] there) that one may not divide sacrifices against sacrifices or a meal-offering against a meal-offering, and it derives this from [the verse], "To all the sons of Aaron it shall be, each man like his brother" [Leviticus 7:10]. Furthermore, [the Gemara] raises an objection there from [the teaching], "The modest ones withdraw their hands, and the gluttons divide [it]" — [and answers,] "What does 'divide' mean? They snatch [it]," etc. And Rabbi [my master] says that division and casting lots are not effective for them such that it becomes one's [private] property with which to betroth a woman or to exact it through judges; however, nevertheless they would cast lots to give each one his portion, lest they quarrel together, as it is written (Hosea 4[:4]): "And your people are like those who contend with a priest." And as for that which [the Gemara] answers there that "divide" is not literal, rather [it means] they snatch — and it does not answer thus [i.e., that they cast lots] — it is because "divide" implies that they compel [each other] to divide; therefore, [it explains it as] because they snatch those [portions] that are not theirs. [From my master.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:1:1.hebrew: ניפרוס סודרא עליה אתי למסחטיה - מכאן מייתי ר"ת ראיה דביין ושמן לא שייכא סחיטה; לעיל בשלהי שמונה שרצים (שבת דף קיא. בד"ה האי מסוכרייתא) פירשתי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:1:1.english: "Let us spread a cloth over it — he will come to squeeze it" - From here Rabbeinu Tam brings a proof that [regarding] wine and oil, [the prohibition of] squeezing does not apply; [as] I explained above at the end of [the chapter] Shemonah Sheratzim (Shabbat 111a, s.v. Hai mesukhreita).

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:2:1.hebrew: לא מספקין ולא מטפחין - לא כפי' הקונטרס, משום דא"כ מאי איריא ביו"ט? אפי' בחול המועד נמי אסור, כדתנן במועד קטן פרק בתרא (דף כח:): "נשים במועד מענות, אבל לא מטפחות". אלא נראה לרבי: משום שמחה רגילין לספק ולטפח בהשמעת קול, ואסור שמא יתקן כלי שיר, כדמפרש בהמוצא תפילין (עירובין דף קד.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:2:1.english: "One may not clap [hands] or strike [one's body]" - [This is] not like the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi, who explained it as referring to mourning], because if so, why does it specifically state [that it is forbidden] on a Festival? Even on Chol HaMoed it is also forbidden, as we learned in a Mishnah in the last chapter of Moed Katan (28b): "Women on the Festival [i.e., Chol HaMoed] may wail, but they may not clap [in mourning]." Rather, it appears to the Rabbi: out of joy, people are accustomed to clap and slap to produce a sound, and it is forbidden lest one repair a musical instrument, as [the Gemara] explains in [the chapter entitled] HaMotzei Tefillin (Eruvin 104a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:4:1.hebrew: וכן היה הלל אומר - מתניתין כרבנן דפליגי עליה באיזהו נשך (ב"מ ד' עה.), וקי"ל כוותייהו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:4:1.english: "And thus Hillel would say" - [Our Mishnah is] like the Rabbis who disagree with him in [chapter] Eizehu Neshech (Bava Metzia 75a), and we hold [in accordance with them].

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:6:1.hebrew: רבה אמר ניתנה ליתבע - הלכה כרבה לגבי רב יוסף, ורב אויא ורבה בר עולא מחמרי אנפשייהו. כ"ה בס"א: "דאי אמרת ניתנה ליתבע אתי למיכתב" — אע"פ שמזכיר לו לשון שאלה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:6:1.english: Rabba said: It can be claimed - The halakha follows Rabba against Rav Yosef, and Rav Avya and Rabbah bar Ulla were [merely] being stringent upon themselves. So it is in other texts: "For if you say it can be claimed, he will come to write" — even though he uses the language of "borrowing" [with him]:

Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:9:1.hebrew: דאיגלאי מילתא דבחול הויא - ורב יוסף לא מיירי אלא בשבת ויו"ט ודאי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 148b:9:1.english: For it became clear that it was on a weekday - And Rav Yosef is speaking only of a definite Shabbat or Festival:
